title: Dispatch CSA 5: Missing Pages Found in Returned Navigator's Log
summary: A concealed record describes the choice made beside the black stone.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Institute last night released six pages removed from the returned Mr. Rook’s navigation log. They were found sewn into the lining of his coat after a nurse noticed that he slept with it under his pillow. Their account differs from the one the returnees first gave.

According to the pages, the earlier survey found the brass anchor already assembled beside the black stone. A note in Professor Vey’s hand instructed them to set it. The party followed those directions, though the professor now living in the Institute says he has never written the note. Once the anchor engaged, the aperture began opening at several positions and dates at once.

Miss Quill stayed at the stone while the other three fled toward one opening. The returned Mr. Rook wrote that she volunteered to hold the release lever until they had crossed. The last entry reads: “We saw her let go. The water came up in a single wall. We did not see what became of her.” The returnees had reported her dead because they could not imagine anyone surviving it.

Dr. Marr has sent the pages to the party in the Stratum. In a reply received late this afternoon, Miss Quill said the black stone bears no assembled anchor, no note, and no sign that anyone has yet crossed the plain. “Then this is our chance,” she said.

The returned Mr. Rook, confronted with the released pages, told our reporter that he hid them because he feared the younger party would refuse to go to the stone. “If they turn back,” he said, “we may be the only people who ever learn how many doors it can open.” He then asked that the interview be ended.
